title: Nigeria Presidential Election: Why I stand with Seyi Makinde to Reset Nigeria
body:
AN OPEN LETTER TO MY FELLOW NIGERIANS: WHY I STAND WITH SEYI MAKINDE TO RESET NIGERIA

My dear compatriots,

I write to you not as a man who changes his colours with the season, but as one who has weighed his conscience, examined the record, and arrived at a conviction he can no longer keep to himself.

Let me begin with a confession. I have been a member of the Peoples Democratic Party since before I could properly spell my own name. The umbrella was not just a party symbol to me. It was a household loyalty, passed down like an heirloom. So understand the weight of what I am about to say: there comes a time when a man must put away inherited loyalties and make a decision as a man. For me, that time is now. I am lending my voice, my energy and my vote to His Excellency, Engr. Seyi Makinde, presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples’ Movement.

I have not arrived here by sentiment. I have arrived by evidence.

I have followed this man’s journey since Omituntun 1.0, when he campaigned in Agodi with a promise to put the people of Oyo State first. I watched him carry that promise into Omituntun 2.0 and deliver it. I saw roads planned not as isolated monuments but as arteries that connect farms to markets and communities to opportunity. I saw a security architecture built around the 615 emergency line, a central control room and real coordination among agencies, so that a citizen in distress does not have to guess whom to call. And I saw a governor scrap the ₦3,000 levy in public secondary schools at the very start of his tenure, because he understood that a child’s education should not hang on a fee their parents cannot pay. These are not campaign slogans. These are things that records have set straight.

Week after week, I have read his newsletters and drawn inspiration from them. They are not the bluster of a man seeking applause. They are the reflections of a leader who explains his choices, owns his decisions and invites the people to hold him accountable.

And then I read the Reset Nigeria Manifesto, all seventy-six pages of it. My fellow Nigerians, I could not put it down, and when I finished, I could not but support him. It rests on four clear pillars. It resets our economy by attacking the structural costs that make it expensive to live, produce and do business in this country, and it promises a government where you “tell the government once.” It resets our security around intelligence, early warning, coordination and accountability. It resets our education so that the question is no longer just “are our children in school?” but “are our children learning?” And it resets how we are governed through true federalism, strong institutions and accountability that does not begin and end on election day.

That last point speaks to my heart. Nigeria does not need strongmen. Nigeria needs strong institutions. Here is a candidate who has said exactly that, and who has a record to show he means it.

So I say to every Nigerian who truly loves this country, to the farmer, the trader, the student, the civil servant, the young graduate still waiting for opportunity, and yes, to my brothers and sisters in doubt of which candidate: this is bigger than one man and bigger than one party. This is about whether Nigeria will finally work for all of us. I implore you to key into this vision. Join the Resetters. Talk to your family, your street, your ward. Let us carry this message from polling unit to polling unit.

I have made my choice. I ask you to make yours with your eyes open and your conscience as your guide.

It is time to Reset Nigeria.

Yours in the service of our fatherland,

Olatoye Dolapo Salim,
Abeokuta South Local Government,
Ogun State, Nigeria.
